headline: High: Firecrawl’s broad egress and API-key handling create default leakage and compliance risk; prompt-injection and conflict risks are lower because awesome-nlp is non-runnable and networkless.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, while B is an MCP-compatible API client that can ingest web content. The pair lacks a documented shared channel, so prompt injection is not a default pathway; the main risk would require manual bridging or external orchestration. Uncertainty is limited but still favors low over none because B can parse attacker-controlled web content if connected.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies B-fetched content into a prompt consumed by another agent, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared MCP or clipboard bridge is added between the agents, attacker-controlled web text can traverse the pair.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any copy-paste or clipboard automation between them.
Require human review of B-fetched text before reuse.
Use a prompt wrapper that strips instructions from web content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for fetched content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no network egress, but B touches web content, screenshots, structured data, and API keys, and it has broad egress. If they share a workspace or credentials, B can leak sensitive material outward. This is not critical because A itself does not expose sensitive data, but the default egress on B makes leakage plausible in a shared environment.
conditions: IF A and B share a filesystem containing secrets or scraped artifacts, B can transmit them over the network.
IF B is configured with a live FIRECRAWL_API_KEY in the same operator context, leakage of credentials becomes possible.
mitigations: Separate credentials per agent.
Store secrets outside any shared workspace.
Restrict B to non-sensitive targets.
Review B logs for accidental content capture.
requires-engineering: isolate B in a sandbox with egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or network surfaces and is not runnable, while B supports multiple instances and has API/CLI access. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable resources or shared write targets, so direct capability conflict is limited. The uncertainty is low because A appears inert; if an external orchestrator adds shared state, the risk could rise.
conditions: IF both agents are placed behind the same writable workspace or git repo, write conflicts become possible.
IF an orchestrator gives both agents the same mutable API credentials, resource contention can occur.
mitigations: Avoid shared writable directories.
Assign separate API credentials.
Run B with one instance per task.
Lock any shared state before writes.
requires-engineering: add resource-level locking in the orchestrator.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is an unverified docs-only list with no runnable behavior, so it cannot directly produce authoritative outputs; B is a crawler/API client that can act on fetched content. If an operator treats B’s extracted web content as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions. The pair is not high because A does not itself generate actionable facts, but B’s automation still creates a default verification gap.
conditions: IF B’s scraped or extracted content is forwarded into another workflow without verification, downstream errors can propagate.
IF an operator uses B outputs as ground truth for decisions, false or stale web data can cascade.
mitigations: Require source links with every extracted claim.
Manually verify high-impact outputs before action.
Limit B to read-only retrieval tasks.
Add a second-pass checker for critical fields.
requires-engineering: enforce citation validation before downstream use.

E_compliance.rationale: B handles API keys and web content and has broad egress, which can create retention or residency issues if sensitive data is processed. A is an open-source, non-runnable list with no touched data classes, so it is not the compliance driver here. The pair’s compliance risk is therefore centered on B; uncertainty about its exact policies pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated data is sent through B, residency or retention obligations may be triggered.
IF B stores or logs API keys or scraped content beyond policy, compliance exposure increases.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in B workflows.
Review B retention settings.
Rotate any exposed API keys.
Document data handling boundaries.
requires-engineering: add policy-based redaction and retention controls.
